new.n: Elk Rapids (first town laid out in Boone County)
new.v: Coins, tokens, household items from the old town
new.st: Elk Rapids stood on the east bank of the Des Moines River in section 34, T82N R26W, named for the shallow rapids where elk crossed. In 1855 it had three stores and dwellings for 150 people, a mill and a post office; a freshet carried the mill away in 1857 and the town declined. The schoolhouse at the foot of the hill stood until 1870. 'No one could now tell by looking at the site of Elk Rapids that a village ever stood there.' The Elk Rapids bridge keeps the name.

new.st: Mining town on sections 15, 16 and 22 of Hampton Township (T18N R1E), where Heagy & Stoddard and Taylor Williams worked coal; at one time it had about 1,000 people. A railroad to the mines was built in the winter of 1872-73 to the Western Union line at Watertown. Extinct by 1908.

new.n: Coltonville (first county seat of DeKalb County)
new.v: Coins, tokens, household items from the old town
new.st: Coltonville, on the bluff overlooking the rapids of the west fork of the South Branch of the Kishwaukee near the site of an old Indian town, was where the first DeKalb County court met in a hewed-log cabin; a 'paper town' rival of Centerville, Brush Point and Sycamore. Pin at GNIS Coltonville School (historical).

vs-1999563.st: Village with a 100-barrel flouring mill (1875), a Methodist church and its own string band; it 'went down' when the Great Western railroad passed it by.

vs-2000450.st: Geneva was laid out in 1836 by Dr. Eli Reynolds and Harvey Gillett about three miles up the river from Muscatine, in Sweetland Township; Reynolds got a bill through the 1837-38 legislature to make it the county seat, but the governor never signed it. Extinct by 1911.

xr-mann-valley-church.st: A second, older burial ground, Old Mann Valley Cemetery (Find a Grave 2346708, 21 memorials, burials from about 1855; the Mann family came in 1853), lies about 1.7 km away at 44.8730,-92.7067. It is also look-only.
